example_usages: Errani & Vavassori win mixed doubles title [TournamentVictoryEvent] --winner--> Sara Errani [Person] || 2024 US Open prize money distribution [PrizeMoneyDistributionEvent] --winner--> Aryna Sabalenka [Person]
model_justification: The schema.org property winner has a specific domain of LoseAction, which does not fit PrizeMoneyDistributionEvent or TournamentVictoryEvent.

schema_definition: Organizations that the person works for.
example_usages: Piers Harding-Rolls [Person] --worksFor--> Ampere Analysis [Organization] || Romain Montbabut [Person] --worksFor--> Benoît Castel [Person]
model_justification: Person works for another Person (acting as an employer/organization), fitting worksFor. | The property 'worksFor' is a direct and perfect match for the relation and signature.

schema_definition: A set of Category Code values.
example_usages: "NOVA classification system" (Entity) as CategoryCodeSet
model_justification: CategoryCodeSet explicitly mentions 'classification system' and 'taxonomy' in its definition, making it a perfect match.

schema_definition: A date value in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).
example_usages: "2012" (Entity) as Date || "Saturday" (Entity) as Date
model_justification: The OIE type 'Date' aligns with schema.org's 'Date' datatype, representing specific calendar days, months, or years. | The OIE type 'Date' is defined as a particular day, month, and year, which directly matches the schema.org 'Date' datatype, despite some mentions being 'DayOfWeek'.

schema_definition: A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes. Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured. Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA" Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Regio
example_usages: "half the nation" (Entity) as DefinedRegion || "Colombia's coffee-growing region" (Entity) as DefinedRegion
model_justification: The OIE type 'GeographicArea' includes both administrative and non-administrative regions, making schema.org's 'DefinedRegion' the best fit for its flexibility. | The schema.org 'DefinedRegion' class is the best fit as it covers geographic areas defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, which aligns with examples like 'western Colombia' and 'Colombia's coffee-growing region'.
judge_notes: "half the nation" is a vague extent; DefinedRegion is for shipping and delivery regions.

schema_definition: Properties that take Distances as values are of the form '<Number> <Length unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 ft'.
example_usages: "1,300km" (Entity) as Distance
model_justification: The OIE type and mentions directly refer to a numerical value representing length or extent of space, which matches schema.org Distance.

schema_definition: A governmental organization or agency.
example_usages: "French health ministry" (Entity) as GovernmentOrganization || "authorities" (Entity) as GovernmentOrganization
model_justification: The OIE type 'GovernmentMinistry' is a department of government, which is a specific type of schema.org 'GovernmentOrganization'. | schema.org/GovernmentOrganization is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and 'authorities'.

schema_definition: Data type: Integer.
example_usages: "four people" (Entity) as Integer || "11 people" (Entity) as Integer
model_justification: 'PopulationCount' refers to a whole numerical value representing individuals, which directly matches the schema.org Integer data type.
judge_notes: "four people" is a counted quantity with a unit, not a bare integer literal.

schema_definition: A News/Media organization such as a newspaper or TV station.
example_usages: "AFP" (Entity) as NewsMediaOrganization || "BBC News" (Entity) as NewsMediaOrganization
model_justification: The OIE type 'NewsAgency' is explicitly listed as an alias for schema.org's 'NewsMediaOrganization'. | The OIE type 'NewsOrganization' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'NewsMediaOrganization'.

schema_definition: A sports club.
example_usages: "PSG" (Entity) as SportsClub
model_justification: The OIE type 'SportsClub' directly matches schema.org's definition, and 'Barcelona' and 'PSG' are prominent sports clubs.

schema_definition: The author of this content or rating. Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably.
example_usages: Marca's statement on 'kings of all-time' [Statement] --author--> Marca [Newspaper]
model_justification: The Newspaper is the author of the statement, so the inverse of `author` is appropriate.

schema_definition: The place where the person was born.
example_usages: Luis Felipe Molina [Person] --birthPlace--> Manizales [City]
model_justification: schema:birthPlace directly expresses the place of origin for a person.

schema_definition: A category for the item. Greater signs or slashes can be used to informally indicate a category hierarchy.
example_usages: Wood Mackenzie [Organization] --category--> research and consulting company [OrganizationType]
model_justification: The 'category' property provides a general classification for diverse entities.

schema_definition: A citation or reference to another creative work, such as another publication, web page, scholarly article, etc.
example_usages: Dream: attack cost collapsed, defense cost stable [StatementOnAttackDefenseCosts] --citation--> blog post by Dream [Publication]
model_justification: The 'Statement on attack defense costs' (CreativeWork) is attributed to a 'blog post by Dream' (Publication, a CreativeWork), fitting a citation relationship.

schema_definition: The person or organization who wrote a composition, or who is the composer of a work performed at some event.
example_usages: Castel created "bread of yesterday and tomorrow" [ProductCreationEvent] --composer--> Benoît Castel [Person]
model_justification: ProductCreationEvent is an Event, and Person is the creator, fitting composer (broadly interpreted).
judge_notes: composer is for musical and written compositions; the object created a loaf of bread.

schema_definition: The basic containment relation between a place and one that contains it.
example_usages: Manizales [City] --containedInPlace--> Colombia's coffee-growing region [DefinedRegion]
model_justification: schema:containedInPlace directly expresses that a place is located within a larger place.

schema_definition: The specific time described by a creative work, for works (e.g. articles, video objects etc.) that emphasise a particular moment within an Event.
example_usages: Official says burned area looks like "war zone" [Statement] --contentReferenceTime--> Monday [TemporalExpression]
model_justification: `contentReferenceTime` indicates the specific date and time described or emphasized within the content of a creative work, aligning with 'at time' for reports, statements, and forecasts.

schema_definition: The date on which the CreativeWork was created or the item was added to a DataFeed.
example_usages: Historic Ciphers [CipherDocumentType] --dateCreated--> Ancient Greece and Rome [HistoricalPeriod]
model_justification: No schema.org property fits the 'dates back to' relation for a document type and historical period.

schema_definition: The expected departure time.
example_usages: Swift left event after midnight [Departure] --departureTime--> Star-studded New York event [SocialEvent]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The object is the event departed from, not a time.

schema_definition: A director of e.g. TV, radio, movie, video gaming etc. content, or of an event. Directors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.
example_usages: The Odyssey [Movie] --director--> Christopher Nolan [FilmDirector]
model_justification: The 'director' property directly links a Movie to the Person who directed it.

schema_definition: The class of drug this belongs to (e.g., statins).
example_usages: Jack Antonoff [Person] --drugClass--> Friend [Role]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Jack Antonoff --drugClass--> Friend" is nonsensical.

schema_definition: The duration of the item (movie, audio recording, event, etc.) in [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).
example_usages: 500 Symbol Extract [DocumentSection] --duration--> 29 Minutes [Duration]
model_justification: No schema.org property fits the 'in' relation for a document section and a duration.
judge_notes: Object is the reporting period, not the item's own running length.

schema_definition: Medical expert advice related to the plan.
example_usages: Mayor Brown urges vigilance and patience [PublicAdvisory] --expertConsiderations--> public [GroupOfPeople]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A Diet property linking a public advisory to its audience.

schema_definition: Represents a relationship between two geometries (or the places they represent), relating a geometry to another that geospatially overlaps it, i.e. they have some but not all points in common. As defined in [DE-9IM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DE-9IM).
example_usages: Spain [Country] --geoOverlaps--> France [Country]
model_justification: The 'geoOverlaps' property implies sharing common points (like a border), which fits the meaning of 'is neighboring' for countries.
judge_notes: Spain and France do not geospatially overlap; the text asserts adjacency.

schema_definition: A Category code contained in this code set.
example_usages: NOVA classification system [CategoryCodeSet] --hasCategoryCode--> ultraprocessed [FoodProcessingLevel]
model_justification: The 'hasCategoryCode' property indicates that a category code set includes a category code, and FoodProcessingLevel is a type of DefinedTerm, which is a supertype of CategoryCode.

schema_definition: Points-of-Sales operated by the organization or person.
example_usages: Benoît Castel [Person] --hasPOS--> patisseries [FoodEstablishment]
model_justification: Person operates a FoodEstablishment (Place), fitting hasPOS.

schema_definition: A contact location for a person's residence.
example_usages: Angélica Ávila [Person] --homeLocation--> hotel [Building]
model_justification: schema:homeLocation expresses a person's residential place, which aligns with 'stayed in' for a temporary residence.

schema_definition: A diagnostic test that can identify this sign.
example_usages: 10 [Quantity] --identifyingTest--> Ebola [InfectiousDisease]
model_justification: No schema.org property directly links a Quantity (representing testing entities) to an InfectiousDisease for what is currently tested for.
judge_notes: "10 --identifyingTest--> Ebola" is nonsensical.

schema_definition: Indicates an item or CreativeWork that this item, or CreativeWork (in some sense), is part of.
example_usages: AI tool developed for Descrypt project [AIToolDevelopment] --isPartOf--> Descrypt Project [ResearchProject]
model_justification: The 'isPartOf' property is a general fit for a creative work (development/compilation) being part of a larger creative work (research project).

schema_definition: The organization issuing the item, for example a [[Permit]], [[Ticket]], or [[Certification]].
example_usages: Authorities order evacuations near Toledo [EvacuationOrder] --issuedBy--> authorities [GovernmentOrganization]
model_justification: The 'issuedBy' property fits for an official order being issued by an organization.

schema_definition: Whether the legislation is currently in force, not in force, or partially in force.
example_usages: Spokane County Sheriff John Nowels [Person] --legislationLegalForce--> Spokane County [AdministrativeArea]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Sheriff --legislationLegalForce--> Spokane County" is nonsensical.

schema_definition: An Organization (or ProgramMembership) to which this Person or Organization belongs.
example_usages: Stéphanie Rist [Person] --memberOf--> French health ministry [GovernmentOrganization]
model_justification: The schema.org property 'memberOf' (Person -> Organization) accurately describes a person being a minister of a government organization.

schema_definition: The larger organization that this organization is a [[subOrganization]] of, if any.
example_usages: department of pediatrics [OrganizationalDepartment] --parentOrganization--> Children’s Hospital Los Angeles [Hospital]
model_justification: The 'parentOrganization' property correctly models a sub-organization (department) being part of a larger organization (hospital).

schema_definition: A link to the ListItem that precedes the current one.
example_usages: Governor Ferguson requests federal assistance [RequestEvent] --previousItem--> Governor Ferguson speaks with President Trump [CommunicationEvent]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: Used to sequence two events; previousItem is scoped to ListItem.

schema_definition: The service provider, service operator, or service performer; the goods producer. Another party (a seller) may offer those services or goods on behalf of the provider. A provider may also serve as the seller.

model_justification: The various statements, beliefs, and descriptions (CreativeWorks) are provided by 'experts', 'AICompany', 'Person', 'GovernmentOrganization', 'GovernmentOfficial' (Organizations/Persons).
judge_notes: The person is making the claim, not providing a service.

schema_definition: The "spatial" property can be used in cases when more specific properties (e.g. [[locationCreated]], [[spatialCoverage]], [[contentLocation]]) are not known to be appropriate.
example_usages: Russian tanks in Ukraine's capital [ImageContent] --spatial--> Ukraine's capital [City]
model_justification: The place is the general spatial context for the image content.

schema_definition: The spatialCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the place(s) which are the focus of the content. It is a subproperty of contentLocation intended primarily for more technical and detailed materials. For example with a Dataset, it indicates areas that the dataset describes: a dataset of New York weather would have spatialCoverage which was the place: the state of New York.
example_usages: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo [DiseaseOutbreak] --spatialCoverage--> three eastern provinces [AdministrativeAreaGroup]
model_justification: The 'spatialCoverage' property indicates the geographic focus or scope of a creative work or event, which aligns with the meaning of 'restricted to' a specific area.

schema_definition: The (e.g. fictional) character, Person or Organization to whom the quotation is attributed within the containing CreativeWork.
example_usages: Buyers will maintain reserves [PolicyForecast] --spokenByCharacter--> June Goh [Person]
model_justification: The 'spokenByCharacter' property is the closest for attributing a statement to a person, generalizing its domain from 'Quotation'.

schema_definition: A sub property of participant. The sports team that participated on this action.
example_usages: Neymar finishes career as top goalscorer [CareerAchievementEvent] --sportsTeam--> Brazil [SportsTeam]
model_justification: The 'sportsTeam' property links an exercise action (or related event) to the sports team involved, fitting 'for team'.

schema_definition: A subject of the study, i.e. one of the medical conditions, therapies, devices, drugs, etc. investigated by the study.
example_usages: Ebola treatments trial [MedicalTrial] --studySubject--> two antiviral drugs [DrugClass]
model_justification: The 'studySubject' property indicates the medical entity being investigated by a medical study (MedicalTrial), directly fitting 'tests'.

schema_definition: An Event that is part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each of which is a subEvent of the conference.
example_usages: Neymar's 2026 World Cup appearances [TournamentAppearance] --subEvent--> Neymar scores goal against Norway [GoalScoringEvent]
model_justification: The 'subEvent' property indicates that a larger event encompasses smaller component events, which fits the 'includes' relation.

schema_definition: A CreativeWork or Event about this Thing.
example_usages: Rumored wedding celebrations kick off [SocialEvent] --subjectOf--> Mason realized event was real due to street closures [Realization]
model_justification: The 'subjectOf' property directly matches the meaning of an entity being the topic or focus of a creative work or event.

schema_definition: The "temporal" property can be used in cases where more specific properties (e.g. [[temporalCoverage]], [[dateCreated]], [[dateModified]], [[datePublished]]) are not known to be appropriate.
example_usages: Xbox shuttered four studios in 2024 [BusinessEvent] --temporal--> 2024 [Year]
model_justification: The 'temporal' property is a general temporal relation for events, fitting 'Year' as text.

schema_definition: A sub property of location. The final location of the object or the agent after the action.
example_usages: large area of high pressure [WeatherSystem] --toLocation--> Portugal [Country]
model_justification: No existing schema.org property directly links a weather system to its geographical direction of development.
judge_notes: A pressure system over Portugal is a location, not the endpoint of a MoveAction.

schema_definition: An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/04/16/announcing-schema-org-actions/) and [Actions overview document](https://schema.org/docs/actions.html).
example_usages: "innovates and steps up its attacks" (Entity) as Action
model_justification: The schema.org Action class is the most general and appropriate fit for the OIE_TYPE 'Action' and its examples.

schema_definition: A chemical substance is 'a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types' (source: [ChEBI:59999](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=59999)).
example_usages: "sugar" (Entity) as ChemicalSubstance
model_justification: Most examples like 'sugar', 'sodium', and 'fats' are chemical substances, making this the most specific and appropriate fit.

schema_definition: A public structure, such as a town hall or concert hall.
example_usages: "roads" (Entity) as CivicStructure
model_justification: Roads and highways are public structures intended for public use, fitting schema.org/CivicStructure.

schema_definition: A collection of items, e.g. creative works or products.
example_usages: "allies’ stockpiles" (Entity) as Collection
model_justification: The schema.org Collection class is the best fit for 'Inventory' as a grouping of items, such as 'stockpiles' or 'arsenal'.

schema_definition: A college, university, or other third-level educational institution.
example_usages: "University of Oxford" (Entity) as CollegeOrUniversity
model_justification: The schema.org CollegeOrUniversity class is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE, definition, and the mention 'University of Oxford'.

schema_definition: Event type: Conference event.
example_usages: "Critical NATO summit in Turkey" (Event) as ConferenceEvent
model_justification: The schema.org ConferenceEvent class perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its example of an 'international summit'.

schema_definition: A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what the term is about.
example_usages: "seafarers’ safety" (Entity) as DefinedTerm
model_justification: The OIE type 'Concept' and its examples, representing abstract ideas, are well-matched by schema.org's 'DefinedTerm', which is used for vocabulary terms and concepts.

schema_definition: The act of departing from a place. An agent departs from a fromLocation for a destination, optionally with participants.
example_usages: "Strategic Retreats" (Entity) as DepartAction
model_justification: 'Strategic Retreats' are a type of military movement or departure, which aligns well with 'DepartAction'.

schema_definition: A class of medical drugs, e.g., statins. Classes can represent general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, common physiological effects, etc.
example_usages: "two antiviral drugs" (Entity) as DrugClass
model_justification: The schema.org DrugClass is a direct and perfect match for the OIE_TYPE, definition, and the mention 'two antiviral drugs'.
judge_notes: "two antiviral drugs" are drug instances, not a pharmacological class.

schema_definition: Event type: Education event.
example_usages: "Castel discovered breadmaking" (Event) as EducationEvent
model_justification: The OIE type 'SkillDiscovery' is a form of learning or an educational experience, fitting schema.org's 'EducationEvent'.

schema_definition: An event happening at a certain time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Ticketing information may be added via the [[offers]] property. Repeated events may be structured as separate Event objects.
example_usages: "Deaths" (Entity) as Event
model_justification: The OIE type 'EventType' refers to general occurrences like 'Deaths' or 'wildfire', which are best categorized by the broad schema.org 'Event' class.

schema_definition: A food-related business.
example_usages: "patisseries" (Entity) as FoodEstablishment
model_justification: The OIE type 'Establishment' with the example 'patisseries' is best represented by schema.org's 'FoodEstablishment', a local business primarily involved in food services.

schema_definition: A hospital.
example_usages: "Children’s Hospital Los Angeles" (Entity) as Hospital
model_justification: Hospital is a direct and perfect match for the OIE type and its example.

schema_definition: An image file.
example_usages: "openly-accessible satellite imagery" (Entity) as ImageObject
model_justification: The schema.org 'ImageObject' is the most appropriate general class for 'Imagery' as visual representations, covering all mentions.

schema_definition: An infectious disease is a clinically evident human disease resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents, like pathogenic viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi, protozoa, multicellular parasites, and prions. To be considered an infectious disease, such pathogens are known to be able to cause this disease.
example_usages: "Ebola" (Entity) as InfectiousDisease
model_justification: The schema.org InfectiousDisease class is a specific and accurate match, as all mentions ('Ebola', 'flu', 'malaria') are examples of infectious diseases.

schema_definition: A medical trial is a type of medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or medical procedures. In general, medical trials are controlled and subjects are allocated at random to the different treatment and/or control groups.
example_usages: "Ebola treatments trial" (Entity) as MedicalTrial
model_justification: The schema.org MedicalTrial class explicitly includes 'clinical trial' as an alias and perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and mention.

schema_definition: A publication containing information about varied topics that are pertinent to general information, a geographic area, or a specific subject matter (i.e. business, culture, education). Often published daily.
example_usages: "Marca" (Entity) as Newspaper
model_justification: The schema.org `Newspaper` class directly matches the OIE_TYPE definition and 'Marca' is an example of a newspaper.

schema_definition:
Data type: Number.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
example_usages: "34 locations" (Entity) as Number
model_justification: The schema.org Number class is the most appropriate for the examples, which are all numerical counts of discrete items.
judge_notes: "60,000 people" carries a unit; Number is the bare literal datatype.

schema_definition: Entities that have a somewhat fixed, physical extension.
example_usages: "burned area" (Entity) as Place
model_justification: `Place` is a broad category for geographical locations, which perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its diverse mentions like states and specific areas.

schema_definition: The act of planning the execution of an event/task/action/reservation/plan to a future date.
example_usages: "Conspiracy among Allies" (Entity) as PlanAction
model_justification: A 'conspiracy' or 'plot' is a type of secret planning action, which aligns well with 'PlanAction'.

schema_definition: A Research project.
example_usages: "Descrypt Project" (Entity) as ResearchProject
model_justification: The schema.org 'ResearchProject' class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE and the mention 'Descrypt Project'.

schema_definition: Enumerates common size groups for various product categories.
example_usages: "toddler" (Entity) as SizeGroupEnumeration
model_justification: AgeGroup is a type of classification group, and SizeGroupEnumeration includes age-related examples like 'Adult' and 'Kids'.
judge_notes: "toddler" read as a clothing size group; the text means a young child.

schema_definition: A stadium.
example_usages: "Miami Stadium" (Entity) as StadiumOrArena
model_justification: The OIE type 'Stadium' directly matches schema.org's 'StadiumOrArena' definition, and 'Miami Stadium' is an example.

schema_definition: Lists or enumerations dealing with status types.
example_usages: "Undeciphered Status" (Entity) as StatusEnumeration
model_justification: The schema.org 'StatusEnumeration' class is a direct and accurate match for the OIE_TYPE 'Status' and the mention 'Undeciphered Status'.
judge_notes: "Undeciphered Status" is a status value, not an enumeration type.

schema_definition: A vehicle is a device that is designed or used to transport people or cargo over land, water, air, or through space.
example_usages: "fighter jets" (Entity) as Vehicle
model_justification: The schema.org Vehicle class perfectly matches the OIE_TYPE and its examples of transportation devices.

schema_definition: A WebSite is a set of related web pages and other items typically served from a single web domain and accessible via URLs.
example_usages: "museum website" (Entity) as WebSite
model_justification: The OIE type 'Website' is a direct and perfect match for schema.org's 'WebSite' class.

judge_notes: "parents --contraindication--> fruit snacks".

schema_definition: The date on which the CreativeWork was created or the item was added to a DataFeed.

schema_definition: A director of e.g. TV, radio, movie, video gaming etc. content, or of an event. Directors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

schema_definition: The distance travelled, e.g. exercising or travelling.

schema_definition: Someone working for this organization.

schema_definition: A resource from which this work is derived or from which it is a modification or adaptation.

model_justification: Date is the schema.org data type for specific calendar dates, which matches all mentions including relative and absolute dates. | Mentions are ISO 8601 calendar dates without time, matching the Date datatype. | Mentions are calendar dates, aligning with schema.org's Date data type. | Mentions are specific calendar dates, aligning with schema.org's Date datatype. | The OIE_TYPE 'Date' and mentions '2026-07' and '2025' match schema.org Date as calendar date representations. | The examples include calendar dates (e.g., '2026-07-05') and years ('2010'), aligning with the schema.org Date class for
judge_notes: "Sunday" is typed as an ISO 8601 date value.

schema_definition: A software application.
example_usages: "Nano Banana 2" (Entity) as SoftwareApplication || "Artificial intelligence" (Entity) as SoftwareApplication || "Transkribus" (Entity) as SoftwareApplication
model_justification: Artificial intelligence and tools like Transkribus align with software applications for task execution. | The schema.org SoftwareApplication class best fits the computational system definition and the product name example 'Nano Banana 2'.
judge_notes: "Artificial intelligence", a field of study, is typed as an application.

schema_definition: Other co-agents that participated in the action indirectly. E.g. John wrote a book with *Steve*.
domain_range_violations: Event --participant--> DefensiveTechnology || UserInteraction --participant--> Person || Event --participant--> Organization
example_usages: Russian attack on Kyiv on 2026-07-01 [Event] --participant--> Geran-4 UAV [DefensiveTechnology] || Trump-Zelensky phone call on 2026-07-05 [UserInteraction] --participant--> Volodymyr Zelensky [Person] || Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo [Event] --participant--> Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale [Organization]
model_justification: The schema.org 'participant' property directly matches the 'SocialEvent → Person' signature, representing indirect involvement in an action. | fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: The production company or studio responsible for the item, e.g. series, video game, episode etc.
example_usages: Production of Spider-Man: Brand New Day [PublicationEvent] --productionCompany--> $225 million [MonetaryAmount] || Avengers: Endgame [Movie] --productionCompany--> Marvel Studios [Corporation] || Double Fine Productions [Organization] --productionCompany--> Psychonauts [Product]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate | productionCompany fits Organization → Product

schema_definition:
Data type: Number.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
example_usages: "71%" (Entity) as Number || "4,800 jobs" (Entity) as Number || "11" (Entity) as Number
model_justification: 93, 11, 4, 66,000, and 605 are all pure numerical values matching schema.org's Number data type. | Mentions are pure numerical values without units, matching schema.org Number's representation of numeric values. | Percentages and numerical values align with the schema.org Number type for measurable quantities. | Schema.org Number (datatype) is the best fit for percentage values like '40%'.

schema_definition: The amount of money.
example_usages: 2025 US Open Singles Prize Award [SportsTournamentPrizeAward] --amount--> £3.74m ($5m) [MonetaryAmount] || US Open Prize Money Increased by 39% Since 2024 [PrizeMoneyIncrease] --amount--> £2.84m ($3.6m) [MonetaryAmount] || 2025 US Open Singles Prize Award [SportsTournamentPrizeAward] --amount--> £115,000 [MonetaryAmount]
model_justification: Schema.org 'amount' fits SportsTournamentPrizeAward/PrizeMoneyIncrease to MonetaryAmount in prize distribution context.

schema_definition: Organization: A business corporation.
example_usages: "Universal Pictures" (Entity) as Corporation || "Dream" (Entity) as Corporation || "Marvel Studios" (Entity) as Corporation
model_justification: Schema.org Corporation is a specific type of Organization that aligns with the definition and examples of business entities. | The OIE_TYPE 'Company' and mentions 'Dream' and 'Financial Times' fit schema.org Corporation as legal business entities.

schema_definition: A museum.
example_usages: "Lalique museum" (Entity) as Museum || "Louvre museum" (Entity) as Museum
model_justification: Schema.org's Museum class matches the definition and examples of a public institution for preserving/exhibiting artifacts.

schema_definition: Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.
example_usages: "Psychonauts" (Entity) as Product || "peanut butter puffs" (Entity) as Product || "pain du coin" (Entity) as Product
model_justification: Examples are specific software/games offered for sale, matching schema.org Product. | Mentions are food items offered for sale, matching schema.org's Product definition. | Schema.org Product encompasses all examples, including food items like 'fruit pouches'.

schema_definition: Quantities such as distance, time, mass, weight, etc. Particular instances of say Mass are strings like '3 kg' or '4 milligrams'.
example_usages: "650" (Entity) as Quantity || "220,000" (Entity) as Quantity || "3,000" (Entity) as Quantity
model_justification: Quantity represents measurable numerical values, fitting the mention '650' as a standalone count. | The mentions '220,000', '2,500 firefighters', etc., represent measurable numerical values, matching the schema.org Quantity data type.

schema_definition: Event type: Social event.
example_usages: "Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's rumored wedding event" (Event) as SocialEvent || "Rumored pre-party at Madison Square Garden" (Event) as SocialEvent
model_justification: A pre-party is a social gathering for entertainment. | Weddings are social gatherings for interaction and celebration.

schema_definition: An Event that is part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each of which is a subEvent of the conference.
example_usages: Additive impact on gut microbiome [ScientificStudy] --subEvent--> Elizabeth Dunford [Person] || Toddler food processing analysis [ScientificStudy] --subEvent--> United States [Country] || Daily Cyberattacks from China [CyberAttackStats] --subEvent--> AI Agent Cyberattack on Taiwan [CyberAttack]
model_justification: No schema.org property directly represents a wildfire cluster/event including another wildfire event; a new property is needed. | The 'subEvent' property is used in inverse to indicate the cyberattack is a component of the statistics. | fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: A movie.
example_usages: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" (Entity) as Movie || "Avengers: Endgame" (Entity) as Movie || "Spider-Man: No Way Home" (Entity) as Movie
model_justification: Schema.org Movie matches the definition and examples provided, which are all titles of films.

schema_definition: A tourist attraction. In principle any Thing can be a [[TouristAttraction]], from a [[Mountain]] and [[LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings]] to a [[LocalBusiness]]. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristAttraction]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist attraction properties to any other type. (See examples below)
example_usages: "Wingen-sur-Moder" (Entity) as TouristAttraction
model_justification: TouristAttraction fits as a specific place of interest, aligning with the example 'Wingen-sur-Moder' as a location drawing visitors.
judge_notes: "Wingen-sur-Moder" is a town.

schema_definition: Indicates an item or CreativeWork that this item, or CreativeWork (in some sense), is part of.
domain_range_violations: HistoricalTextDecryption --isPartOf--> Hackathon || SportsEvent --isPartOf--> SportsEvent || Country --isPartOf--> Continent
example_usages: AI Chatbot Deciphers Borg Cipher [HistoricalTextDecryption] --isPartOf--> Descrypt Project Develops AI Tool [Hackathon] || AI Decodes Charles V's Letter [HistoricalTextDecryption] --isPartOf--> Descrypt Project Develops AI Tool [Hackathon] || Brazil vs Norway World Cup Round of 16 [SportsEvent] --isPartOf--> 2026 World Cup [SportsEvent]
model_justification: Reused 'isPartOf' as-is (Country is part of Continent). | Schema.org's isPartOf property indicates that an item is part of a larger creative work or event, aligning with the observed Project → Hackathon and HistoricalTextDecryption → Hackathon relations. | Using isPartOf to indicate a sports event is part of a larger tournament.

schema_definition: A pointer to another, somehow related product (or multiple products).
example_usages: ultraprocessed foods [FoodCategory] --isRelatedTo--> 71% [Number] || Ukraine attacks Russian oil refineries [MilitaryAttackEvent] --isRelatedTo--> Russia attacks Ukraine's cities and energy facilities [MilitaryAttackEvent] || Amy Coleman's Memo on Industry Changes [CompanyFocusOnCustomerAreas] --isRelatedTo--> Microsoft Job Cuts and Xbox Restructuring [JobCutsAndRestructuring]
model_justification: The 'isRelatedTo' property generically connects two Things, suitable for linking events to related events regardless of type. | The 'isRelatedTo' property is a general association for 'Country → CyberAttackAttribution'. | fallback: top candidate | isRelatedTo fits Product/Service → Product/Service
judge_notes: schema.org isRelatedTo links related products or services.

schema_definition: A sub property of participant. The winner of the action.
domain_range_violations: SportsTeam --winner--> SportsTeam || SportsTeam --winner--> WorldCupVictory || Person --winner--> SportsMedal
example_usages: Spain's World Cup champions [SportsTeam] --winner--> Argentina [SportsTeam] || Spain’s women’s side [SportsTeam] --winner--> Spain’s women’s 2023 World Cup victory [WorldCupVictory] || Neymar [Person] --winner--> 2012 silver medal [SportsMedal]
model_justification: Reusing winner in inverse direction as the goal scoring action is a type of winning in the context of a sports event. | Using winner as the property for a person winning a medal in a competition. | fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Spain's World Cup champions --winner--> Argentina" names the loser as winner.

schema_definition: A contact location for a person's place of work.
example_usages: Benoît Castel [Person] --workLocation--> Paris [Place] || Benoît Castel [Person] --workLocation--> La Grande Epicerie de Paris [Restaurant] || Benoît Castel [Person] --workLocation--> Hotel Costes [Restaurant]
model_justification: Schema.org's workLocation property (Person→Place) fits Person→TouristAttraction as a professional location. | The 'workLocation' property matches the Person → Place signature. | The 'workLocation' property matches the Person → Restaurant signature.

schema_definition: A point value or interval for product characteristics and other purposes.
example_usages: "8,700 hectares" (Entity) as QuantitativeValue || "36C to 37C" (Entity) as QuantitativeValue || "40C" (Entity) as QuantitativeValue
model_justification: No schema.org class directly represents area measurements; mentions require a QuantitativeValue subclass. | No schema.org class directly represents temperature measurements; mentions require a Quantity subclass.

schema_definition: The specific time described by a creative work, for works (e.g. articles, video objects etc.) that emphasise a particular moment within an Event.
domain_range_violations: WildfireEvent --contentReferenceTime--> Date || Schedule --contentReferenceTime--> Event || ServicePeriod --contentReferenceTime--> Organization
example_usages: Wildfires in France [WildfireEvent] --contentReferenceTime--> 2026-07-25 [Date] || 22 June to 28 June [Schedule] --contentReferenceTime--> France records 2,025 excess deaths during June heatwave [Event] || first 1,000 days of a child’s life [ServicePeriod] --contentReferenceTime--> Healthy Babies Bright Futures [Organization]
model_justification: Reused 'contentReferenceTime' as-is (Schedule describes time of Event). | WildfireEvent (CreativeWork) → Date (DateTime) aligns with 'contentReferenceTime's domain/range. | fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The subject is an event, not a creative work describing a time.

schema_definition: Upcoming or past event associated with this place, organization, or action.
example_usages: Lionel Messi [Person] --event--> Spain's 2026 World Cup victory [WorldCupVictory] || Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's rumored wedding event [SocialEvent] --event--> Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $26m charity donation [Event] || Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's rumored wedding event [SocialEvent] --event--> America's 250th birthday [Event]
model_justification: The schema.org 'event' property aligns with both 'SocialEvent → Event' and 'SocialEvent → SocialEvent' signatures as a general event association. | fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: A member of this organization.
example_usages: Xbox Studio Spin-Offs [StudioSpinOff] --members--> Double Fine Productions [Organization] || Xbox Studio Spin-Offs [StudioSpinOff] --members--> Undead Lab [Organization] || Xbox Studio Spin-Offs [StudioSpinOff] --members--> Compulsion Games [Organization]
model_justification: members applies to Organization → Person
judge_notes: Superseded plural, and the subject is a spin-off event rather than an organization.

schema_definition: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the receiving end of the action.
example_usages: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $26m charity donation [Event] --recipient--> Nashville [Place] || Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's $26m charity donation [Event] --recipient--> Kansas City [Place] || 2025 US Open Mixed Doubles Prize Award [SportsTournamentPrizeAward] --recipient--> Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori [SportsTeam]
model_justification: Schema.org 'recipient' matches SportsTournamentPrizeAward to SportsEvent/Team as prize recipients. | The schema.org 'recipient' property directly matches the 'Event → Place' signature for entities receiving a donation or benefit.

schema_definition: The start date and time of the item (in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).
example_usages: 16 large wildfires active in Washington state [WildfireClusterEvent] --startDate--> 2026-08-04 [Date] || Washington state wildfires cause evacuations of 60,000 people [WildfireEvacuation] --startDate--> 2026-08-03 [Date] || World Confectioner of the Year [Event] --startDate--> 2026-07-14 [Date]
model_justification: The 'startDate' property fits the Event → Date signature directly. | The evacuation and cluster events' dates align with 'startDate' as temporal markers for events.

schema_definition: The instant the event occured.
example_usages: Ukraine attacks Russian oil refineries [MilitaryAttackEvent] --timestamp--> 2026-08-05T20:00:00 [DateTime] || Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo [Event] --timestamp--> 2026-07-01 [Date] || AI Agent Cyberattack on Taiwan [CyberAttack] --timestamp--> 2026-07 [Date]
model_justification: The 'timestamp' property captures the specific DateTime of an InstantaneousEvent, which includes the MilitaryAttackEvent subtype. | The 'timestamp' property is used in inverse to indicate when the attack was performed. | fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: A sub property of instrument. An object used (but not consumed) when performing instructions or a direction.
example_usages: Artificial intelligence [SoftwareApplication] --tool--> Descrypt Project Develops AI Tool [Hackathon] || Transkribus [SoftwareApplication] --tool--> AI Decodes Von Wandersleben's Letter [HistoricalTextDecryption] || Artificial intelligence [SoftwareApplication] --tool--> AI Decodes Borg Cipher [HistoricalTextDecryption]
model_justification: Schema.org's tool property can be applied to a SoftwareApplication used in a process or event.
judge_notes: The project used the AI, not the reverse.

schema_definition: A [hackathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackathon) event.
example_usages: "Descrypt Project Develops AI Tool" (Event) as Hackathon
model_justification: The example 'Descrypt Project Develops AI Tool' aligns with a collaborative tech development event.
judge_notes: A funded research project is typed as a hackathon.

schema_definition: A restaurant.
example_usages: "La Grande Epicerie de Paris" (Entity) as Restaurant || "new venue in Paris" (Entity) as Restaurant || "Hotel Costes" (Entity) as Restaurant
model_justification: Mentions are specific food-related businesses, aligning with schema.org's Restaurant as a subtype of FoodEstablishment.

schema_definition: A person that acts as performing member of a sports team; a player as opposed to a coach.
example_usages: Spain [Country] --athlete--> Spain's World Cup champions [SportsTeam] || Spain [Country] --athlete--> Spain’s women’s side [SportsTeam]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Rodri --athlete--> victory parade" puts an event in the athlete slot.

schema_definition: The place where the person was born.
example_usages: Neymar [Person] --birthPlace--> Brazil [Country] || Benoît Castel [Person] --birthPlace--> Brittany [Place]
model_justification: The 'birthPlace' property aligns with the Person → Place signature. | Using birthPlace to indicate the country where the person was born.

schema_definition: A secondary contributor to the CreativeWork or Event.
example_usages: Descrypt project [Project] --contributor--> Beáta Megyesi [Person] || Descrypt project [Project] --contributor--> Michelle Waldispühl [Person]
model_justification: Schema.org's contributor property indicates secondary participation in a project, aligning with the observed relations.

schema_definition: Indicates an item or CreativeWork that is part of this item, or CreativeWork (in some sense).
example_usages: Copiale cipher [ArchiveComponent] --hasPart--> 105-page manuscript [ArchiveComponent] || Daily Cyberattacks from China [CyberAttackStats] --hasPart--> AI Agent Cyberattack on Taiwan [CyberAttack]
model_justification: Schema.org's hasPart property indicates a part-whole relationship between ArchiveComponents. | The 'hasPart' property is used in inverse to indicate the cyberattack is part of the statistics.

schema_definition: The object that helped the agent perform the action. E.g. John wrote a book with *a pen*.
example_usages: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's rumored wedding event [SocialEvent] --instrument--> white canopy tent [PhysicalObject] || Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's rumored wedding event [SocialEvent] --instrument--> large white staircase prop [PhysicalObject]
model_justification: The schema.org 'instrument' property fits the 'SocialEvent → PhysicalObject' signature for objects used during an action.

schema_definition: Of a [[Person]], and less typically of an [[Organization]], to indicate a topic that is known about - suggesting possible expertise but not implying it. We do not distinguish skill levels here, or relate this to educational content, events, objectives or [[JobPosting]] descriptions.
example_usages: Dan Marks [Person] --knowsAbout--> Long-Term Hormuz Strait Concerns [SecurityRiskAssessment] || Adi Imsirovic [Person] --knowsAbout--> Oil Market Irreversibly Changed [EnergyMarketAnalysis]
model_justification: Reused schema.org/knowsAbout with as_is direction since Person → Analysis fits the domain/range of Organization/Person → Thing.

schema_definition: The total number of individuals that may attend an event or venue.
example_usages: Lalique museum [Museum] --maximumAttendeeCapacity--> 650 [Quantity] || Washington state wildfires cause evacuations of 60,000 people [WildfireEvacuation] --maximumAttendeeCapacity--> 60,000 people [StatisticalPopulation]
model_justification: Schema.org's maximumAttendeeCapacity (Place→Integer) fits Museum→Quantity as a capacity measure. | The evacuation event's evacuee count aligns with the attendee capacity schema.org property, as both relate to a numeric population affected.

schema_definition: The number of employees in an organization, e.g. business.
example_usages: Microsoft Job Cuts and Xbox Restructuring [JobCutsAndRestructuring] --numberOfEmployees--> 4,800 jobs [Number] || Microsoft [Organization] --numberOfEmployees--> 9,000 jobs [Number]
model_justification: numberOfEmployees fits Organization → Number and JobCutsAndRestructuring → Number

schema_definition:
The offer price of a product, or of a price component when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

Usage guidelines:

* Use the [[priceCurrency]] property (with standard formats: [ISO 4217 currency format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217), e.g. "USD"; [Ticker symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cryptocurrencies) for cryptocurrencies, e.g. "BTC"; well known names for [Local Exchange Trading Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_exchange_trading_system) (LETS)
example_usages: Australian Open 2025 [SportsEvent] --price--> £47m [MonetaryAmount] || US Open [SportsEvent] --price--> £67.3m ($90m) [MonetaryAmount]
model_justification: Schema.org 'price' aligns with SportsEvent to MonetaryAmount for prize money values in event context.

schema_definition: The number or other unique designator assigned to a Report by the publishing organization.
example_usages: Ebola case in Haut-Uele province [Event] --reportNumber--> AFP [Organization] || Ebola case in Tshopo province [Event] --reportNumber--> Reuters [Organization]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Ebola case --reportNumber--> AFP"; reportNumber takes a designator string.

schema_definition: A modifiable or non-modifiable factor that increases the risk of a patient contracting this condition, e.g. age, coexisting condition.
example_usages: AI tool could spread misinformation [MisinformationRisk] --riskFactor--> Henk van Ess [Person] || AI erodes trust in satellite imagery [TrustErosion] --riskFactor--> Bill Greer [Person]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: riskFactor is scoped to MedicalCondition.

schema_definition: A pointer from a newer variant of a product to its previous, often discontinued predecessor.
example_usages: Activision-Blizzard [Organization] --successorOf--> Xbox 2024 Staff Reductions [JobCutsAndRestructuring] || Google retracts AI tool [ProductRetraction] --successorOf--> Nano Banana 2 [SoftwareApplication]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate | successorOf inverse fits JobCutsAndRestructuring → Organization
judge_notes: "Google --successorOf--> Earth AI tool".

schema_definition: The "temporal" property can be used in cases where more specific properties (e.g. [[temporalCoverage]], [[dateCreated]], [[dateModified]], [[datePublished]]) are not known to be appropriate.
example_usages: Jewelry theft at Lalique museum [Event] --temporal--> Sunday [Date] || Jewelry theft at Lalique museum [Event] --temporal--> 5:30 am [Time]
model_justification: Schema.org's temporal property accommodates Event→Date/Time as a general temporal relation.

schema_definition: A geographical region, typically under the jurisdiction of a particular government.
example_usages: "Kharkiv region" (Entity) as AdministrativeArea || "Chocó province" (Entity) as AdministrativeArea
model_justification: Bashkortostan, Yaroslavl, Kharkiv region, and Dnipropetrovsk region are all administrative divisions within countries. | Mentions like 'Chocó province' fit schema.org AdministrativeArea as a governed geographical region.

schema_definition: An intangible type to be applied to any archive content, carrying with it a set of properties required to describe archival items and collections.
example_usages: "Copiale cipher" (Entity) as ArchiveComponent || "105-page manuscript" (Entity) as ArchiveComponent
model_justification: Historical ciphers are archival items with encoded content, fitting schema.org's ArchiveComponent.

schema_definition: A chemical substance is 'a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types' (source: [ChEBI:59999](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=59999)).
example_usages: "artificial colorings" (Entity) as ChemicalSubstance || "saturated fats" (Entity) as ChemicalSubstance
model_justification: Schema.org ChemicalSubstance matches examples like 'sodium' and 'emulsifiers' as specific substances.

schema_definition: One of the continents (for example, Europe or Africa).
example_usages: "Europe" (Entity) as Continent
model_justification: Schema.org's Continent class matches the OIE_TYPE definition and the mention 'Europe'.

schema_definition: A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see Chapter 5.4 of ISO 8601).
example_usages: "17:30 ET" (Entity) as DateTime || "2026-08-05T20:00:00" (Entity) as DateTime
model_justification: 2026-08-05T20:00:00 is a specific point in time with both date and time components as defined by schema.org's DateTime. | Examples include specific time points with time zones.

schema_definition: A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes. Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured. Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA" Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Regio
example_usages: "42,000 hectares" (Entity) as DefinedRegion || "Var region" (Entity) as DefinedRegion
model_justification: The mention '42,000 hectares' refers to a measurable geographic region, aligning with the schema.org DefinedRegion class for non-political regions. | The mentions 'Gironde region' and 'Var region' refer to non-sovereign administrative regions within a country, fitting the schema.org DefinedRegion class.
judge_notes: "42,000 hectares" is an area measurement, not a defined region.

schema_definition: Properties that take Distances as values are of the form '<Number> <Length unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 ft'.
example_usages: "1,300km" (Entity) as Distance || "37 miles" (Entity) as Distance
model_justification: 1,300km and 700km are numerical values with units of length fitting schema.org's Distance class. | Distance matches the numerical value with unit in '37 miles', representing a measurable length.

schema_definition: An enterprise (potentially individual but typically collaborative), planned to achieve a particular aim. Use properties from [[Organization]], [[subOrganization]]/[[parentOrganization]] to indicate project sub-structures.
example_usages: "Descrypt project" (Entity) as Project
model_justification: The mention 'Descrypt project' fits schema.org's Project class as a collaborative initiative.

schema_definition: A PublicationEvent corresponds indifferently to the event of publication for a CreativeWork of any type, e.g. a broadcast event, an on-demand event, a book/journal publication via a variety of delivery media.
example_usages: "Production of Spider-Man: Brand New Day" (Event) as PublicationEvent
model_justification: Schema.org PublicationEvent aligns with the example of movie production as a release event.
judge_notes: Film production is typed as a publication event.

schema_definition: A screening of a movie or other video.
example_usages: "Minions & Monsters domestic performance" (Event) as ScreeningEvent || "Toy Story 5 domestic performance" (Event) as ScreeningEvent
model_justification: Schema.org ScreeningEvent aligns with the examples of movie showings and box office performance.
judge_notes: A box-office performance figure is typed as a screening.

schema_definition: A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[Statisti
example_usages: "60,000 people" (Entity) as StatisticalPopulation || "1,500 inhabitants" (Entity) as StatisticalPopulation
model_justification: Mentions are numerical counts of people, aligning with statistical population definitions. | StatisticalPopulation represents a set of instances (e.g., people) for analysis, fitting the numerical mention '1,500 inhabitants' as a population group.
judge_notes: "60,000 people" is a count, not a constrained set definition.

schema_definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].
example_usages: "Trump-Zelensky phone call on 2026-07-05" (Event) as UserInteraction
model_justification: Phone calls between leaders qualify as user interactions, though the examples are non-digital. schema.org's UserInteraction is the broadest fit among outdated candidates.
judge_notes: A phone call between heads of state typed as a web-page interaction.

schema_definition: Specifies the Person that is legally accountable for the CreativeWork.
example_usages: King [Organization] --accountablePerson--> Asha Sharma [Person]
model_justification: accountablePerson fits Organization → Person

schema_definition: An actor, e.g. in TV, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.
example_usages: Production of Spider-Man: Brand New Day [PublicationEvent] --actors--> Zendaya [Person]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: Superseded plural form.

schema_definition: An organization that this person is affiliated with. For example, a school/university, a club, or a team.
example_usages: June Goh [Person] --affiliation--> Sparta [Organization]
model_justification: Reused schema.org/affiliation with as_is direction since Person → Organization aligns with the property's definition.
judge_notes: The subject is an economic-benefit node, not a person.

schema_definition: A person or organization attending the event.
example_usages: Israel [Country] --attendee--> US-Israel War on Iran [MilitaryConflict]
model_justification: Minted because no existing schema.org property fits the Country → MilitaryConflict signature as an as_is or inverse.
judge_notes: A country is put in the attendee slot of a clinical trial.

schema_definition: The author of this content or rating. Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably.
example_usages: Sigismund Heusner von Wandersleben [Person] --author--> AI Decodes Von Wandersleben's Letter [HistoricalTextDecryption]
model_justification: Schema.org's author property indicates the creator of a CreativeWork, which can include a HistoricalTextDecryption.
judge_notes: He authored the letter, not the decryption event.

schema_definition: Awards won by or for this item.
example_usages: Spain's World Cup champions [SportsTeam] --awards--> World Cup trophy [AwardTrophy]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: Superseded plural form, and the range is Text.

schema_definition: The cause of a medical condition.
example_usages: Outbreak of Bundibugyo virus in DR Congo [Event] --cause--> Bundibugyo virus species [InfectiousAgentClass]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The outbreak-to-pathogen usage is apt despite the MedicalCondition domain.

schema_definition: The condition, complication, symptom, sign, etc. caused.
example_usages: Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv [Event] --causeOf--> Russia [Country]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "attack on Kyiv --causeOf--> Russia" reverses cause and agent.

schema_definition: A colleague of the person.
example_usages: Benoît Castel [Person] --colleagues--> Romain Montbabut [Person]
model_justification: The 'colleagues' property aligns with the Person → Person signature for professional peers.
judge_notes: Superseded plural form.

schema_definition: A competitor in a sports event.
example_usages: US Open [SportsEvent] --competitor--> Aryna Sabalenka [Person]
model_justification: Schema.org 'competitor' fits SportsEvent to Person for athlete participation in tournaments.

schema_definition: The basic containment relation between a place and one that contains it.
example_usages: artificial colorings [ChemicalSubstance] --containedIn--> ultraprocessed foods [FoodCategory]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: containedIn is Place to Place; used for a substance inside a food category.

schema_definition: The creator/author of this CreativeWork. This is the same as the Author property for CreativeWork.
example_usages: pain du coin [Product] --creator--> Benoît Castel [Person]
model_justification: Reusing 'creator' in inverse direction to fit Product → Person.

schema_definition: The group the release is credited to if different than the byArtist. For example, Red and Blue is credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", but by Lady Gaga.
example_usages: Consumer Brands Association defends toddler foods [IndustryStatement] --creditedTo--> Consumer Brands Association [IndustryAssociation]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A MusicRelease credit property used for who issued a statement.

schema_definition: The date/time the message was received if a single recipient exists.
example_usages: Pedro Sanchez [Person] --dateReceived--> Spain's World Cup champions [SportsTeam]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Pedro Sanchez --dateReceived--> Spain's World Cup champions".

schema_definition: The end date and time of the item (in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).
example_usages: Neymar [Person] --endDate--> Brazil [Country]
model_justification: Using endDate as the property for the retirement event, aligning with the subject (Person) and object (Country).

schema_definition: The most generic uni-directional social relation.
example_usages: Spain's World Cup champions [SportsTeam] --follows--> Fountain collapse in Ciudad Rodrigo [TragicIncident]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: schema.org follows is a social relation between people.

schema_definition: A person or organization who founded this organization.
example_usages: Common Space [Organization] --founder--> Bill Greer [Person]
model_justification: The founder property links an organization to its founder (Person/Organization), so we use it with inverse direction for Person → Organization.

schema_definition: The place where the Organization was founded.
example_usages: hackers [Organization] --foundingLocation--> China [Country]
model_justification: The 'foundingLocation' property fits the 'Organization → Country' signature for origin.

schema_definition: The Person's occupation. For past professions, use Role for expressing dates.
example_usages: Romain Montbabut [Person] --hasOccupation--> head baker [Occupation]
model_justification: The 'hasOccupation' property directly matches the Person → Occupation signature.

schema_definition: A common representation such as a protein sequence or chemical structure for this entity. For images use schema.org/image.
example_usages: Volodymyr Zelensky [Person] --hasRepresentation--> Zelensky’s plea for NATO air defense support [Statement]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A BioChemEntity property linking a person to his own statement.

schema_definition: Used to indicate a specific claim contained, implied, translated or refined from the content of a [[MediaObject]] or other [[CreativeWork]]. The interpreting party can be indicated using [[claimInterpreter]].
example_usages: Kevin Feige on Spider-Man's debut [Statement] --interpretedAsClaim--> Kevin Feige [Person]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The range is Claim; the object is the speaker.

schema_definition: A pointer to another product (or multiple products) for which this product is a consumable.
example_usages: pain du coin [Product] --isConsumableFor--> Salish salt [FoodIngredient]
model_justification: The 'isConsumableFor' property fits the Product → FoodIngredient signature.
judge_notes: The salt is consumed for the bread, not the reverse.

schema_definition: Indicates a BioChemEntity that is (in some sense) a part of this BioChemEntity.
example_usages: saturated fats [ChemicalSubstance] --isPartOfBioChemEntity--> ultraprocessed foods [FoodCategory]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The part-hood is right; the BioChemEntity scoping is not.

schema_definition: Identifies the issue of publication; for example, "iii" or "2".
example_usages: Asha Sharma [Person] --issueNumber--> Asha Sharma's Note on Xbox Restructuring [XboxReset]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Asha Sharma --issueNumber--> her note on the restructuring".

schema_definition: The person or organization that countersigned the legislation. Depending on the legal context, a countersignature can indicate that the signed authority undertakes to assume responsibility for texts emanating from a person who is inviolable and irresponsible, (for example a King, Grand Duc or President), or that the authority is in charge of the implementation of the text.
example_usages: United States [Country] --legislationCountersignedBy--> Iran-US MoU on Strait of Hormuz [MemorandumOfUnderstanding]
model_justification: Reused schema.org/legislationCountersignedBy with as_is direction since Country → MemorandumOfUnderstanding aligns with Legislation → Organization/Person.
judge_notes: The memorandum is countersigned by the state, not the reverse.

schema_definition: An individual or organization that has some kind of responsibility for the legislation. Typically the ministry who is/was in charge of elaborating the legislation, or the adressee for potential questions about the legislation once it is published.
example_usages: 16 large wildfires active in Washington state [WildfireClusterEvent] --legislationResponsible--> National Weather Service [GovernmentOrganization]
model_justification: The wildfire cluster is warned by a government organization, aligning with 'legislationResponsible' for oversight.
judge_notes: "wildfires --legislationResponsible--> National Weather Service".

schema_definition: The manufacturer of the product.
example_usages: China [Country] --manufacturer--> renewable energy-related components [Product]
model_justification: Reused schema.org/manufacturer with as_is direction since Country → Product aligns with the property's domain/range.

schema_definition: A link to the ListItem that follows the current one.
example_usages: Europe braces for further extreme temperatures this weekend [HeatwaveForecastEvent] --nextItem--> France records 2,025 excess deaths during June heatwave [Event]
model_justification: No schema.org property directly links HeatwaveForecastEvent to Event in this context; minting 'followedBy'.
judge_notes: Used to sequence two events; nextItem is scoped to ListItem.

schema_definition: Things owned by the organization or person.
example_usages: Benoît Castel [Person] --owns--> new venue in Paris [Restaurant]
model_justification: The 'owns' property directly matches the Person → Restaurant signature.

schema_definition: The 90th percentile value.
example_usages: ultraprocessed foods [FoodCategory] --percentile90--> 71% [Number]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A distribution percentile used for a plain proportion.

schema_definition: Event that this person is a performer or participant in.
example_usages: Neymar [Person] --performerIn--> 2026 World Cup [SportsEvent]
model_justification: Using performerIn as the property for a person participating in a sports event.

schema_definition: An organization that acknowledges the validity, value or utility of a credential. Note: recognition may include a process of quality assurance or accreditation.
example_usages: Universal Pictures hits $4B mark [SaleEvent] --recognizedBy--> Universal Pictures [Corporation]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: Credential-recognition property used for a box-office milestone.

schema_definition: The CreativeWork that captured all or part of this Event.
example_usages: NetBlocks [UserBlocks] --recordedIn--> Kherson city blackout [InfrastructureDamageEvent]
model_justification: The 'recordedIn' property links the InfrastructureDamageEvent to the UserBlocks CreativeWork that documented it, matching the reported relation.
judge_notes: NetBlocks recorded the blackout, not the reverse.

schema_definition: The URL at which a reply may be posted to the specified UserComment.
example_usages: Google [Organization] --replyToUrl--> Google retracts AI tool [ProductRetraction]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A comment-reply URL property linking a company to a retraction event.

schema_definition: The response (yes, no, maybe) to the RSVP.
example_usages: Google [Organization] --rsvpResponse--> AI tool could spread misinformation [MisinformationRisk]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Google --rsvpResponse--> AI tool could spread misinformation".

schema_definition: A pointer to products or services sought by the organization or person (demand).
example_usages: Washington State Governor declares statewide emergency [EmergencyDeclaration] --seeks--> US President Donald Trump [Person]
model_justification: The emergency declaration seeks assistance from the president, matching the 'seeks' property for requests.
judge_notes: The range is Demand; the object is the person asked.

schema_definition: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the sending end of the action.
example_usages: Axel Oxenstierna [Person] --sender--> Sigismund Heusner von Wandersleben [Person]
model_justification: Schema.org's sender property links a Message to its originator, aligning with the letter-sending context.

schema_definition: The spatialCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the place(s) which are the focus of the content. It is a subproperty of contentLocation intended primarily for more technical and detailed materials. For example with a Dataset, it indicates areas that the dataset describes: a dataset of New York weather would have spatialCoverage which was the place: the state of New York.
example_usages: Colombian earthquake [Event] --spatialCoverage--> Colombia [Country]
model_justification: spatialCoverage fits Event → City/Country with examples like 'New York State'.

schema_definition: A person or organization that supports a thing through a pledge, promise, or financial contribution. E.g. a sponsor of a Medical Study or a corporate sponsor of an event.
example_usages: Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo [Event] --sponsor--> World Health Organization [Organization]
model_justification: The 'sponsor' property from schema.org has a domain including Event and a range of Organization, which matches the instance 'Ebola treatments trial in DR Congo' (Event) --> 'World Health Organization' (Organization).

schema_definition: The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. E.g. John wrote a book from *January* to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.\n\nNote that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clari
example_usages: Rumored pre-party at Madison Square Garden [SocialEvent] --startTime--> 17:30 ET [DateTime]
model_justification: The schema.org 'startTime' property matches the 'SocialEvent → DateTime' signature for temporal markers.

schema_definition: A medical study or trial related to this entity.
example_usages: Toddler food processing analysis [ScientificStudy] --study--> peanut butter puffs [Product]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The object is what was studied, not a study.

schema_definition: An event that this event is a part of. For example, a collection of individual music performances might each have a music festival as their superEvent.
example_usages: 2024 US Open [SportsEvent] --superEvent--> US Open Prize Money Increased by 39% Since 2024 [PrizeMoneyIncrease]
model_justification: Schema.org 'superEvent' (Event→Event) is used in inverse to map PrizeMoneyIncrease to its prior event.

schema_definition: Indicates a target EntryPoint, or url, for an Action.
example_usages: Russian attack on Kyiv on 2026-07-01 [Event] --target--> Kyiv [City]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate

schema_definition: The total time required to perform instructions or a direction (including time to prepare the supplies), in [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).
example_usages: Toy Story 5 domestic performance [ScreeningEvent] --totalTime--> $1.06 billion [MonetaryAmount]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A duration property carrying a box-office total.

schema_definition: Any FDA or other warnings about the drug (text or URL).
example_usages: Volodymyr Zelensky [Person] --warning--> Russian ballistic missile and drone attack on Kyiv [Event]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: A Drug warning property linking a president to a missile attack.

schema_definition: The size of the business in annual revenue.
example_usages: Minions & Monsters domestic performance [ScreeningEvent] --yearlyRevenue--> $5.8 million [MonetaryAmount]
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: "Russia --yearlyRevenue--> Kherson blackout".

schema_definition: Event type: Conference event.
example_usages: "NATO summit in Ankara" (Event) as ConferenceEvent
model_justification: A NATO summit is a formal international conference, matching schema.org's ConferenceEvent definition with examples like summits and symposiums.

schema_definition: Event type: Food event.
example_usages: "Benoît Castel crowned World Confectioner of the Year" (Event) as FoodEvent
model_justification: Mentions describe a culinary award, fitting schema.org's FoodEvent as a gastronomic activity.
judge_notes: An award ceremony for a confectioner is typed as a food event.

schema_definition: Classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Enumerated type.
example_usages: "Bundibugyo virus species" (Entity) as InfectiousAgentClass
model_justification: The example refers to a virus species, which fits as a subclass of InfectiousAgentClass.

schema_definition: A profession, may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification.
example_usages: "head baker" (Entity) as Occupation
model_justification: Mentions are job roles (e.g., 'head baker'), aligning with schema.org's Occupation definition.

schema_definition: A permit issued by an organization, e.g. a parking pass.
example_usages: "street closure permits" (Entity) as Permit
model_justification: Street closure permits are official authorizations.

schema_definition: Event type: Sales event.
example_usages: "Universal Pictures hits $4B mark" (Event) as SaleEvent
model_justification: Schema.org SaleEvent aligns with the example of hitting a revenue milestone through sales.
judge_notes: A box-office milestone is typed as a sales event.

schema_definition: A schedule defines a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring [[Event]]. At a minimum a schedule will specify [[repeatFrequency]] which describes the interval between occurrences of the event. Additional information can be provided to specify the schedule more precisely. This includes identifying the day(s) of the week or month when the recurring event will take place, in addition to its start and end time. Schedules may also have start and end dates to indicate when they are
example_usages: "22 June to 28 June" (Entity) as Schedule
model_justification: Schema.org's Schedule class represents recurring time periods, fitting the date ranges in the mentions.
judge_notes: Schedule describes a repeating period; this is a single date range.

schema_definition: ServicePeriod represents a duration with some constraints about cutoff time and business days. This is used e.g. in shipping for handling times or transit time.
example_usages: "first 1,000 days of a child’s life" (Entity) as ServicePeriod
model_justification: Schema.org ServicePeriod fits 'first 1,000 days of a child’s life' as a defined duration.

schema_definition: A stadium.
example_usages: "Madison Square Garden" (Entity) as StadiumOrArena
model_justification: Madison Square Garden is a large civic structure for public gatherings.

schema_definition: A point in time recurring on multiple days in the form hh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see [XML schema for details](http://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#time)).
example_usages: "5:30 am" (Entity) as Time
model_justification: Time is the schema.org data type for time of day, which matches the mention '5:30 am' as a specific temporal point.

schema_definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].
example_usages: "NetBlocks" (Entity) as UserBlocks
model_justification: fallback: top candidate
judge_notes: The monitoring organisation NetBlocks typed as a user-blocking interaction.
